gen-silkscreen-gf-alan-sans: Alan Sans keeps its curve tails pulled well back from the body, giving a modern, businesslike text. Silkscreen sits beside it with pixel-spaced, lo-fi swagger, a retro toy next to a tidy colleague.
gen-silkscreen-gf-albert-sans: Albert Sans stays legible even at tiny sizes, its apertures wide open. Silkscreen brings the retro, lo-fi spark while this sans keeps a steady, contemporary hand, and that gap between them is the pair's whole charm.
gen-silkscreen-gf-alef: Silkscreen's lettering is spaced so loosely you can nearly feel the air around each character, with zero stroke modulation. Alef's open-ended curves then read clean and modern in sans-serif text.
gen-silkscreen-gf-alegreya-sans-sc: Retro pixel rope, then a gentler sibling. Silkscreen is best at stamping out lo-fi, rope-like headings with the same line in every stem and tail, while Alegreya Sans SC does its best work with a welcoming gap in the c and a modern, plain sans manner.
gen-silkscreen-gf-almarai: Lo-fi and retro up top, tidy below. Almarai keeps a line width that never swells or tapers, so a long passage in this sans moves along smoothly, with letters that never pinch shut.
gen-silkscreen-gf-amarna: Silkscreen's strongest trait is the space around every letter, like spaghetti laid out in a row. And Amarna answers with contrast-free strokes and unclogged small counters, so this sans keeps the page clean.
gen-silkscreen-gf-andika: Silkscreen lays its lines out like spaghetti, with space around every letter that you can almost feel, giving a lo-fi, retro look. Andika's thick terminals take over below, and Silkscreen earns its keep big and short.
gen-silkscreen-gf-anta: Approachable, with a wire-bent look. Anta's gaping e shapes and constant thickness make a long passage in this plain sans feel professional, while Silkscreen stays retro and lo-fi above it.
gen-silkscreen-gf-antic: Silkscreen goes lo-fi and retro, letters spaced out like spaghetti. Antic sets a drawn-with-one-nib plain sans below, open-mouthed like an unjoined chalk arc, while Silkscreen earns its keep big and short.
gen-silkscreen-gf-ar-one-sans: AR One Sans reads modern and contemporary, its brush ends lifting away before each curve closes. But Silkscreen does its best work as a lo-fi, retro heading, strokes of constant width like bent pipe, while this sans handles the running text.
